answer: Bind each agent identity to one physical secure chip. The chip signs a fresh challenge at registration, and the ledger records its fingerprint once, so a second identity from the same chip gets refused. Voting weight grows only from that chip's verified work history. Faking 10,000 agents would take 10,000 chips at $22 each plus $180,000 in fees, with a 14 day attestation queue before any vote lands. A fake farm faces a hiker's canyon problem. The far side looks close, yet the delta between one real crossing and a thousand pretend ones shows up in the signal the ledger checks.
